Subject: Contract Refresh: Reserved GPUs & Logical Isolation for Greenline Health

Hi Avery —

As Greenline’s renewal approaches, I wanted to propose an amendment that adds a dedicated reserved pool (additional 8x A100-80GB equiv. GPUs) with logical tenant isolation and throughput SLOs to support your expanded inference workload. High-level summary attached (pricing_proposal_v3.pdf).

Key points:
- Reserved pool: 8x GPUs, dedicated node set for Greenline; reserved capacity billed monthly.
- Isolation: logical tenant fencing (namespace + network segmentation), strict KV-cache partitioning, and optional node fencing to prevent cross-tenant noisy neighbors. We can enforce per-tenant quotas and dedicate host-level GPU allocation on request.
- Throughput guarantees: 99th percentile token-latency target of < 200ms for 512-token sequences under steady-state; sustained throughput baseline of 320 requests/min with burst to 500 reqs/min for short periods.
- Term: proposed 12-month renewal with price as in the attached proposal; optional 24-month term discount available.

Questions for you:
1) Would Greenline like the logical isolation only (software-enforced) or node-fenced physical isolation?
2) Any procurement timing constraints or required contract language we should be aware of?

If it helps, Marissa can send the isolation spec and a network diagram for your security team to review. How does next Wednesday (Aug 18) look for a 30-min call to finalize?

Thanks,
Dylan

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear summary and proposal. A few follow-ups from our side before we schedule a call:

- Isolation: Our security team prefers node-fenced physical isolation for production models that handle PHI. Can you confirm whether the 8x reserved pool can be provisioned as physically isolated hosts within our VPC? We also need confirmation on KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and that audit logs are captured for inference requests.

- Throughput/latency: The targets look reasonable. Can you provide empirical numbers from a comparable customer or an internal benchmark for 512-token sequences? We need p95/p99 numbers to map to our SLA.

- Term & billing: Procurement asked whether the billing can be monthly with a 12-month commitment and whether early termination liability changes with node-fencing.

- Compliance artifacts: Please share SOC2 report, pen-test summary, and the isolation spec so we can route to InfoSec.

Can Marissa send the isolation spec and a short network diagram? Also copying Raj from procurement — he’ll coordinate on contract language.

Hi Avery / Raj —

Attaching the isolation spec (redwood_isolation_spec.docx) and a simplified network diagram (greenline_network_diagram.png) for your InfoSec review. High-level notes included below:

- Physical isolation option: we can reserve dedicated hosts (node-fenced) that are placed into your VPC. These hosts will not be used by any other tenant and will have separate NVMe/ephemeral storage etc.
- Logical isolation option: namespace and runtime partitioning with strict KV cache partitioning and per-tenant quotas. CPU/GPU scheduling uses cgroup-based limits.
- KMS/CMEK: supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault. Keys are never escrowed by Redwood.
- Audit & logs: request-level audit logs (request IDs, model variant, timestamp, IP) can be exported to your SIEM; retention configurable per contract.
- Migration window: 2-week scheduled migration; can support a staged rollout and temporary burst capacity for cutover.

Attachments: redwood_isolation_spec.docx (docx, 420KB); greenline_network_diagram.png (PNG, 120KB)

Next steps: if this looks good we can draft an amendment that specifies the node-fenced host count and an effective date. Happy to jump on the Aug 18 call to walk InfoSec through the spec.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
